subsystems.name: Bioink
subsystems.role: printable mixture of living cells and stimuli-responsive materials that forms the structure.
parts: living cells (e.g. stem cells or primary cells)

subsystems.name: Bioprinter
subsystems.role: deposits bioink layer by layer with spatial control over material and cell placement.

subsystems.name: Responsive scaffold
subsystems.role: provides the shape-changing capability through patterned material properties.

subsystems.name: Stimulus control
subsystems.role: triggers the shape change at the desired time and rate.

subsystems.name: Culture and maturation system
subsystems.role: keeps cells alive and allows the construct to mature and remodel.

subsystems.name: Computational design
subsystems.role: predicts how the printed structure will deform over time.

buildSteps.title: Design the transformation
buildSteps.detail: Software simulates how regions of different swelling or stiffness will bend, fold or expand when triggered, and the print pattern is set accordingly.

buildSteps.title: Formulate bioinks
buildSteps.detail: Living cells are mixed with hydrogels and stimuli-responsive polymers so the ink is both printable and gentle on cells.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate the bioprinter
buildSteps.detail: Print pressure, speed and nozzle size are tuned for each ink to give consistent strands and high cell survival.

buildSteps.title: Print the construct
buildSteps.detail: Multiple inks and cell types are deposited layer by layer, creating areas that will respond differently to the same stimulus.

buildSteps.title: Crosslink and stabilise
buildSteps.detail: UV light or chemical agents solidify the printed shape and lock in the patterned properties.

buildSteps.title: Mature in a bioreactor
buildSteps.detail: The construct is incubated with nutrients so cells attach, multiply and lay down their own matrix.

buildSteps.title: Trigger and test
buildSteps.detail: A change in temperature, pH or another stimulus is applied and the shape change is recorded and assessed.

buildSteps.title: Implant or use
buildSteps.detail: For medical use the construct would be placed where it adapts to the body's own conditions, such as a changing pH or temperature.

prerequisites.why: provides the layer-by-layer deposition of living cells and soft materials that 4D builds on.
materials that swell, shrink or change stiffness in response to temperature or pH exist but are not yet reliable inside the body.
supplies the living cells that must survive printing and then function in the construct.
without a blood supply, printed tissue more than a millimetre thick dies before it can mature.
predicting exactly how a printed soft structure will move over time is still difficult.

pathway.milestone: laboratory demonstrations of self-folding cell-laden hydrogels and simple shape changes
pathway.unlocks: proof that printed biological structures can be programmed to move.

pathway.milestone: vascularised 4D bioprinted tissues that survive and function for weeks
pathway.unlocks: thick, living constructs that can respond while remaining alive.

pathway.milestone: implantable devices that adapt to a physiological trigger
pathway.unlocks: smart stents, valves or patches that change with the body rather than being static.

pathway.milestone: adaptive organs that grow or remodel with a patient
pathway.unlocks: treatments for children who outgrow fixed implants, and organs that heal themselves.
